attempts.prompt:
Create one finished animation line-art frame for Wu Yi (吴懿), frame 293 of the approved palm-held miniature talisman boat action. White paper background, refined thin dark gray ink contours, human anatomical drawing, no color fill, no gray wash, no heavy hatching. Target 1920 x 1080 landscape. ONE image, no contact sheet.
REFERENCE ROLES:
3. frame_000303.png is the independently checked line-art STYLE/COSTUME/BOAT DETAIL anchor only. Keep its thin lines, same hand character, same curved sleeve motifs and carved boat cabin design. Do not copy its pose or its object position. The TARGET block frame has priority for pose and object location.
1. wy_full_master_v1.png is the authoritative Wu Yi costume and 2D line style reference. Only her hand and a portion of her forearm/sleeve are visible in this shot; do NOT add her face, torso, full figure or the three-view characters. Her outer robe has a wide, softly rounded hanging sleeve, a pale inner cuff/band and restrained curved linear botanical embroidery. No black leather arm guard, no armor, no bracelet. Adult graceful hand, natural skin volume, normal finger count.
2. block_000293.png is the exact pose and object-placement reference. Ignore ALL typography, rulers, frame number, side panels and explanatory marks. Use only its central action drawing (image rectangle x360 y90 to x1560 y990). Replace its box palm and segmented block fingers with a believable drawn human hand at the SAME wrist angle, palm orientation, finger spread and perspective. The sleeve enters from upper right and the open hand points left. The forearm connects naturally to the palm through the correct sleeve opening. The thumb is above the palm; the four separate fingers point toward the left/lower left and are relaxed, slightly cupped. The palm is visibly supporting the small object, with the fingers open. This is palm presentation immediately before gentle release; not a clenched grip, throwing windup, flick, catch or pinching gesture.
Preserve the miniature boat's diagonal long axis from upper left to lower right across the open hand, its scale relative to the palm, its projected narrow elongated hull shape and actual contact/support relationship from the block drawing. It is a small intricately carved Chinese nutshell boat talisman (核雕小舟), with a simple shallow cabin suggestion in the same compact hull volume; no large ship, no sail, no wing blades, no luminous green crystal, no flame, no explosion. Restrained fine structural lines for hull rim and carved planking, modest carving detail. The object must remain clearly readable above the palm rather than merge into fingers.
Compose the hand, boat and sleeve together as a hand close-up occupying the middle and lower part of the landscape sheet, retaining the same relative spatial arrangement from reference 2. Remove the excess blank instructional layout and leave generous clean white space around the action. The sleeve may continue beyond the right edge, as the forearm is in the original close-up, but do not crop the fingertips or boat tips. Smooth organic skin contours and joint creases, only the necessary sleeve folds. There must be no geometric boxes, cuboid fingers, construction axes, dashed skeletons, labels, text, number, border, watermark or other person. The visible hand and sleeve must be coherent Wu Yi line art, not a filtered rendering or a block diagram.
FRAME-SPECIFIC INSTRUCTION, highest priority for action:
Early palm support: the four fingers are more bent and more foreshortened than the frame303 style reference. The narrow boat is more steeply diagonal and the cupped palm sits further right, exactly like this frame's block. Do not simply repeat frame303's widely extended fingers.
This is precisely frame 293. Use the target block's current pose, not a generic reused hand illustration. Output only the completed line-art image.
